newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields, CDs end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields, CDs end slightly lower.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed a fraction lower due to a lack of new issuances by commercial banks and no specific buying interest after last week's four-day Chusok holiday, dealers said.
The debt market resumed trading on Monday after the Korean Thanksgiving holidays, which began Thursday last week.
They forecast yields on the corporate bonds and CDs would remain weak throughout this week in the absence of demand.
* Overnight average call rate at 18 against 18.5.
Dealers said only some financial houses, including investment trust companies based in Seoul, showed buying interest today.
"About one fourth of the 4.68 trillion won, which had been released by banks during 10 days before Chusok, have been absorbed into banking houses," the Daewoo dealer said.

But dealers forecast the three-year yield would rise next week, given a large amount of new bond issues planned for this month. The Korea Securities Dealers Association approved 2.87 trillion won worth of corporate bond issues this month against 1.95 trillion in September. -- SHIM SUNG-WON (822) 727 5649
